steps.text: A realistic lizard is a living creature with a sculpted head, legs and skin, and my modeling tools can't produce that shape. The closest version they can build is a segmented body that keeps the articulated, side-to-side swing, without legs or a sculpted head. Which version would you like?

args.title: Lizard version
args.question: Which version should I build? The tools cannot model a sculpted lizard with legs and a head, so pick the closest form.

steps.text: Thanks. I'll build the segmented body with common sizes. Because the segments are a print-in-place chain, the plan needs to be approved first. The plan lists each piece and its gaps, and you can edit the sizes before pressing Go.

args.part: Articulated segmented lizard body (no legs, no sculpted head)
assumptions: Ten segments, each 13 mm long on a 15 mm pitch, so the chain is about 150 mm overall with the 0.4 mm joint gap.
Each segment swings side to side about a vertical pin (3 mm) in a socket (3.6 mm) on the neighbor, giving 0.3 mm radial clearance.
Joints are vertical pins only, so the chain moves in the horizontal plane; the tail narrows through the segments by fixed steps, not a loft.
Printed flat on the bed in one job, Bambu P1S, PLA, 0.4 mm nozzle, no supports needed since every joint is a vertical pin with no overhang beyond 45 degrees.
Sizes are common defaults, not measured from any real lizard.
questions: Should the segments taper from head to tail (wider at the head) instead of uniform width?

steps.text:
I built the articulated body as a chain of 10 print-in-place segments with no legs or sculpted head, since the tools can't model a real lizard shape. Each segment swings side to side on a vertical pin in the next segment's socket, and the plan check and gap check both pass with 0.35 mm joint clearance.

**The chain is about 135 mm long, not 150 mm.** To get closer to 150 mm, I can add a segment or two or lengthen the pitch. I also used uniform width, not a taper, and rounded the segment corners by 2.5 mm.

I have not sliced it, so supports and the print time are not yet checked. Each segment is a separate piece on the bed, so one job will print all 10. Tell me if you want me to slice it on the P1S with PLA.
